firewall: R4: the DISCOVERY strand must not read this file.

dataSource.pitDocuments: V10 factor strand private PIT documents (pit_docs.py, companyfacts, filed < t)

population.rule: At cohort date t a frame listing is a member when it has a weekly close exactly at t, listingStart <= t, and the 52 preceding weekly bars are contiguous on the frame calendar (k >= 52, no calendar gap in k-52..k). Listings younger than 52 weeks at t are excluded and counted (IPO-year exclusion).
population.survivorshipGap: see survivorship-gaps-1.0.0.json; coverage vs SEC 10-K filers ~14-17 % (2001-03), ~22 % (2010), ~48 % (2020)

returnBasis.stocks: PRICE_RETURN, entry close week t+1, exit close week t+1+h
returnBasis.benchmark: SPY PRICE_RETURN same dates (context only; classes are cross-sectional)

weighting: equal weight per member within cohort; cohorts equally weighted in means
investmentAssumption: none (no portfolio); E4 compares equal-weight feature top quintile with the equal-weight member population
excessKind: Observed descriptive differences; block-bootstrap intervals over cohort dates and Holm families are given, but nothing here is a tradable excess claim.

resolutionSensitivity.label: POST_HOC_RESOLUTION_SENSITIVITY_NOT_REGISTERED
resolutionSensitivity.reason: registered 1,999 replicates give p >= 1/2000; Holm x 156 >= 0.078, so the registered family cannot reject by construction

pooledProfiles.definition: members in the top quintile (registered direction) of every listed feature; DISTRESSED_REBOUND uses the bottom quintile of vol52w, drawdown52w (i.e. highest volatility, deepest drawdown) and near52wHigh (farthest from the high)

scope: Descriptive anatomy of ex-post winners in a survivor-heavy frame (price return). Separation statistics describe what distinguished winners on average; they are not rules, carry no time-split validation and must not feed the DISCOVERY strand.
